import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Prepare data for visualization
# 1. Top 10 dog breeds
breed_counts = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)

# 2. Age distribution of dogs
age_order = ['0-Jährige', '1-Jährige', '2-Jährige', '3-Jährige', '4-Jährige', 
             '5-Jährige', '6-Jährige', '7-Jährige', '8-Jährige', '9-Jährige', 
             '10-Jährige und älter']
age_counts = df['AlterVHundLang'].value_counts()
age_counts = age_counts.reindex(age_order, fill_value=0)

# 3. District distribution (top 10)
district_counts = df['KreisLang'].value_counts().head(10)

# 4. Gender distribution
gender_counts = df['SexHundLang'].value_counts()

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(20, 16))

# 1. Top breeds - horizontal bar chart
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 1)
bars = ax1.barh(breed_counts.index, breed_counts.values)
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax1.invert_yaxis()
for i, (bar, count) in enumerate(zip(bars, breed_counts.values)):
    ax1.text(count + breed_counts.max()*0.01, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, 
             f'{count:,}', va='center', fontsize=10)

# 2. Age distribution - bar chart
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 2)
bars = ax2.bar(range(len(age_counts)), age_counts.values)
ax2.set_xlabel('Dog Age', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution of Dogs', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax2.set_xticks(range(len(age_counts)))
ax2.set_xticklabels([age.replace('-Jährige', '') for age in age_counts.index], rotation=45, ha='right')
for i, (bar, count) in enumerate(zip(bars, age_counts.values)):
    ax2.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + age_counts.max()*0.01, 
             f'{count:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9, rotation=0)

# 3. District distribution - bar chart
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 3)
bars = ax3.bar(district_counts.index, district_counts.values)
ax3.set_xlabel('District', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('Dog Distribution by District (Top 10)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax3.set_xticklabels(district_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
for i, (bar, count) in enumerate(zip(bars, district_counts.values)):
    ax3.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, bar.get_height() + district_counts.max()*0.01, 
             f'{count:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9, rotation=0)

# 4. Gender distribution - pie chart
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 4)
colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax4.pie(gender_counts.values, labels=gender_counts.index, 
                                   autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=colors,
                                   textprops={'fontsize': 11})
ax4.set_title('Gender Distribution of Dogs', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# Add overall title
plt.suptitle('Zurich Dog Registration Analysis', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor='white')
plt.close()
